Subject: Re: production latency over weekend — request for remediation and credit

Hi Avery,

We experienced repeated high P95 latency on the /generate endpoint during our European peak window (Sat 2028-03-11 18:00 — Sun 2028-03-12 02:00 CET). Our automated order reconciliation jobs retried repeatedly; the result was ~1,200 delayed orders and several customer support escalations. Our telemetry shows baseline P95 ~400ms but spike to 2.4s across multiple shards.

Can you confirm root cause and provide a proposal for financial remediation? Per our contract we expect SLA recourse for sustained latency degradations. We need an interim answer by EOD Monday (18th) so we can update internal stakeholders and Procurement.

Thanks,
Anjali Singh
Head of Platform Reliability — Stellar Retail
anjali.singh@stellar-retail.com
+44 7700 900111

Attachments: SLA-impact-log.txt (attached)
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Anjali Singh <anjali.singh@stellar-retail.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@stellar-retail.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 14:30:12 +0100
Subject: Re: production latency over weekend — request for remediation and credit

Hi Anjali,

Really sorry about the disruption — and thanks for the detailed logs. We immediately throttled background batch workers and rolled a targeted hotfix to the routing logic late Saturday which brought P95 back under 500ms. Root cause (preliminary): a combination of a degraded cache eviction path on the replica set + an orchestration race that led to uneven request distribution during your burst window. Engineering will share a full RCA by Friday.

For next steps on remediation/compensation:
- I'll open a formal Ops ticket and deliver the RCA.
- I will propose a one-off customer concession for the impacted invoice while I get exec sign-off.

Prelim offer (subject to approval): a calculated usage credit tied to the impacted hours + one complimentary service month to offset the operational disruption while you revalidate pipelines. I need approval from finance/legal for the specific numbers; can you confirm your March invoice amount or your average monthly spend so I can surface a concrete dollar figure?

I appreciate the timeline pressure — aiming to get a firm proposal to you by Wed (21st).

Best,
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Account Executive — Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.com

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 10:05:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Stellar — production latency over weekend — proposed concession options

Team — forwarding Stellar's incident and the log. Short summary: 2.4s P95 for critical endpoint during their EU peak causing order delays; customer counts this as an SLA-impact event and has asked for remediation + compensation. They have a committed monthly spend of ~US$12k.

Proposed compensation options (engineering confirmed impact window = ~8 hours of elevated latencies across two burst periods):
A) Credit = 10% of monthly committed spend for March (~$1,200) + one complimentary service month (applied to next renewal).
B) Credit = 6% (~$720) + 10 hours of complimentary priority SRE time for on-site/remote pairing to stabilize integrations.
C) Flat credit $1,000 + expedited support and free trial of our Dedicated routing for 30 days.

Recommendation: Option A (10% + one month). Rationale: proportional to impact, compensates for ops costs, and the one-month credit is a strong signal without materially changing long-term pricing.

Need approvals: Legal (Priyom) — confirm amendment wording for a one-off concession (non-precedent). Finance (Lauren) — confirm we can apply pro-rated credit and one free month in billing system and cap if needed. GTM Exec (Marissa) — sign-off on approach and any caps.

Attachments: credit-calcs-stellar.xlsx (breakdown), hubspot-12345-link.txt

Thanks,
Avery
